title: Nearly 38,000 Jobs Vanish in First Ten Days of May
excerpt: AI-driven restructuring at PayPal, Coinbase, and Cloudflare triggers one of 2026's sharpest early-month job-cut waves
body:
Nearly 38,000 American workers lost their jobs in the first ten days of May 2026, as a cascade of layoff announcements swept through tech, finance, aviation, and media. The cuts mark one of the most concentrated bursts of workforce reduction this year — and AI is the thread running through nearly all of it.

**What happened — the week's biggest cuts:**
Spirit Airlines delivered the single largest blow, accounting for roughly 14,000 job losses after ceasing operations entirely, following prolonged financial distress and weakened demand for ultra-low-cost travel. In tech and finance, PayPal cut 4,760 jobs on May 5, while Coinbase trimmed 700 workers, Freshworks eliminated 500, Arctic Wolf shed 250, and Ticketmaster cut 350 — all in a single week of explicitly AI-justified reductions. Cloudflare followed on May 8, cutting 20% of its staff — roughly 1,100 people — while citing a fundamental shift toward AI-powered operations.

**Why it matters — the AI restructuring signal:**
Andy Challenger of Challenger, Gray and Christmas noted that technology companies are 'leading all industries in layoff announcements' and are 'also often citing AI spend and innovation,' adding that 'regardless of whether individuals are being replaced by AI, the money for these roles is.' His firm reported 83,387 announced U.S. job cuts in April alone — a 38% jump from March's 60,620. Year-to-date, U.S. tech employers have announced 85,411 job cuts from January through April, up 33% from the same period last year.

**What to watch next:**
Indian H-1B visa holders caught in the Coinbase cuts face just 60 days to find new sponsoring employers or exit the country — a pressure point that will intensify if the May wave extends into June earnings season.
